<!--

  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the

Every device except the oldest MyStrom switch returns a type. Before the config flow, the type was not needed. Now it's used to differentiate between a switch and a bulb. To allow the first generation of switches to work again, we set the type to that switch if it's not present.

issue_context.title: Integration Problem with 1st Gen myStrom Adapter
issue_context.body:
### The problem

MyStrom Adapter 1st Generation with Firmware 2.68.10 failes to integration. Only 2nd Generation adapters with temperature sensor works (in my case they have 4.0.7 firmware).

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.7.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2023.6.3

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

mystrom

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/mystrom/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
Old yaml entry, before mystrom was migrated to integration by 2023.7.0

platform: mystrom
name: Hifi Center
host: !secret ip_mystrom_hifi_center
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
2023-07-05 22:26:01.387 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.config_entries] Error setting up entry Hifi Center for mystrom
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/config_entries.py", line 390, in async_setup
    result = await component.async_setup_entry(hass, self)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/mystrom/__init__.py", line 35, in async_setup_entry
    device_type = info["type"]
                  ~~~~^^^^^^^^
KeyError: 'type'
```


### Additional information

_No response_

```
curl --location -g 'http://192.168.1.210/info'  
{"version":"4.0.7","mac":"xxx","ssid":"xxx","ip":"192.168.1.210","mask":"255.255.255.0","gw":"192.168.1.1","dns":"192.168.1.1","static":false,"connected":true,"type":"WS2","name":"WiFi Switch v2 CH","connectionStatus":{"ntp":true,"dns":true,"connection":true,"handshake":true,"login":true}}
```

1st Generation myStrom Adapter delivers the following info:

```
curl --location -g 'http://192.168.1.200/info'

	"mac":	"xxx",

		"handshake":	true,
		"login":	true
	}
}   
```       
I can see, that type is missing on 1st gen adapters. 

Another Issues seams to be, that 1st gen adapter does not respond on http://[device_ip]/api/v1/info request, but 2nd gen is doing. It seams to be, that old 1st gen have a different API as documented here: https://api.mystrom.ch/#rest-api

Any chance to adopt this old type of myStrom Wifi adapter here?

```

      data:
        ip: !secret ip_mystrom_hifi_center
        state: '1'
    turn_off:
      service: rest_command.ecs_generic_relay
      data:
        ip: !secret ip_mystrom_hifi_center
        state: '0'
```

Right, I am trying to look into this but I don't have MyStrom devices so I depend on the help of you.

What I see in the integration is that it is trying to use the `python-mystrom` lib to get device info. 

```python
    try:
        info = await pymystrom.get_device_info(host)
    except MyStromConnectionError as err:
        _LOGGER.error("No route to myStrom plug: %s", host)
        raise ConfigEntryNotReady() from err

    device_type = info["type"]
```
What we at least can see, if there was a connection error, the config entry would throw another error.

When I check the code of `python-mystrom` I see that it first tries to call `http://{host}/api/v1/info`, there's a comment that says "Fall back to the old API version if the device runs with old firmware". And then it tries to do a call to `http://{host}/info.json`. 

In the information I see in this issue I only see calls that go to `/info` and not to `/info.json`. Not sure if that makes a difference, can you maybe try both requests on both devices and post the output here?

EDIT: I also see that previous versions did not call this info endpoint. Probably because the entity type (light/switch) was defined in yaml so it did not have to figure out which type it is.

Could you also please try a request to `http://{host}/api/v1/device/{mac}`?

> When I check the code of python-mystrom I see that it first tries to call http://{host}/api/v1/info, there's a comment that says "Fall back to the old API version if the device runs with old firmware". And then it tries to do a call to http://{host}/info.json.

This was added a while back. It would be that the devices got a firmware update in the meantime or the logic to check for the differences is not as robust as it should be.

Allright, I am now making the exact same conclusion you made haha. Since the `/api/v1/info` call doesn't return a JSON object, it falls back to `info.json`, which works, but doesn't contain a type. That means we need to find another way to identify the device. Or set every device without type as switch, but I am not sure if that's what we want.

To be completely sure, are your devices up to date?

Yes, his devices are up to date. I'm on exactly the same firmware and there's no update available for them, I've just checked.

`"version":	"2.68.10"`

@joostlek 
> Don't forget that companies like you buying the latest version and not an older version haha

Yes but my personal opinion is not to leave customers behind just because they got an older revision of the same product.
I mean it's just an ESP32 implemented in the Gen.2 devices, which you can also modify easily yourself to make it work with HA the way you want without being dependent on the myStrom HA integration. Check [this](https://web.archive.org/web/20211129171915/http://github.com/richardklingler/mystrom) out.
Only thing is you have to find a way to parse the power output from "W" into "kWh" as far as I remember, if you want to integrate the vaules into the HA energy dashboard (most people won't but we are all different). And this should be done on the ESPHome level, not via HA itself, to make it as precise as possible because ESPHome counts the pulses only every second by default I guess.

Edit:
Unfortunately this does not work for Gen.1 devices as they are not based on an ESP32 but this might help someone, maybe also for the future.

Edit2:
In the repo linked above the .yaml code is missing as it's from a deleted GitHub archive. Here's the code you need for ESPHome:

```
esphome:
  name: mystrom-01
  platform: ESP32
  board: esp32doit-devkit-v1

wifi:
  ssid: !secret wifi_ssid
  password: !secret wifi_password

  # Enable fallback hotspot (captive portal) in case wifi connection fails
  ap:
    ssid: "Mystrom Fallback Hotspot"
    password: !secret fallback_password

captive_portal:

# Enable logging
logger:

# Enable Home Assistant API
api:
  password: !secret api_password
ota:
  password: !secret ota_password

i2c:
  sda: 22
  scl: 19
  scan: True

switch:
  - platform: gpio
    name: "myStrom Relay"
    pin: 27
    icon: "mdi:power-socket-fr"
    id: mystrom_relay

# Front red LED
  - platform: gpio
    id: mystrom_red_led
    pin:
      number: 16
      inverted: no
# Front white LED
  - platform: gpio
    id: mystrom_led
    pin:
      number: 17
      inverted: yes

binary_sensor:
# Bottom push button
  - platform: gpio
    pin:
      number: 18
      inverted: yes
    name: "myStrom Button"
    filters:
      - delayed_on: 20ms

# Side push button
  - platform: gpio
    pin:
      number: 23
      inverted: yes
    name: "myStrom Side Button"
    filters:
      - delayed_on: 20ms

sensor:
# Pulses from AD71056 energy meter
  - platform: pulse_meter
    pin: 4
    name: "myStrom Power"
    unit_of_measurement: 'W'
    accuracy_decimals: 3
    filters:
      - multiply: 0.036
    total:
      unit_of_measurement: 'kWh'
      name: 'myStrom Energy'
      accuracy_decimals: 3
      filters:
        - multiply: 0.0000006
  - platform: tmp102
    name: "myStrom Temperature"
    update_interval: 20s

```

I would go to the missing "type" field. If the field isn't there, it's probably one of the oldest MyStrom devices... the 1st Gen Switch. If the "type" field is delivered with an update at some point, that shouldn't be a problem. I hope that MyStrom will then be smart enough to name the type WS1.
